assessment.nobel_worthiness: The optical lattice clock, built on Katori's magic-wavelength proposal, turned optical transitions into frequency standards with fractional uncertainties near 1e-18. It is a clear, original and lasting advance in precision atomic physics, with direct consequences for redefining the second, relativistic geodesy and tests of fundamental constants. Judged from an atomic-physics perspective it is conceptually clean and technically decisive.
assessment.attribution: Katori proposed the magic-wavelength lattice and made the first demonstrations. Ye's group carried strontium lattice clocks to the highest accuracy and stability and developed the comb and cavity-stabilisation tools. A two-person prize looks natural. Single-ion optical clocks (Wineland and others) and the comb work recognised in 2005 are neighbouring achievements that should be acknowledged but do not displace this one.
assessment.maturity: Confirmed independently by many laboratories worldwide, with clocks compared across institutes and continents. The interpretation is stable and the redefinition of the second is under active discussion, so recognition is timely and not premature.
uncertainties: The supplied credit has only two names; other contributors (for example lattice-clock groups beyond these two) may merit consideration, and I have not verified the details of priority.
Overlap with earlier frequency-comb and trapped-ion clock recognition could be argued to dilute novelty.
The date of any formal redefinition of the second is uncertain.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene opened a tunable platform for correlated insulators and superconductivity in flat moire bands. The theoretical prediction of flat bands at a magic angle, followed by the 2018 observation of correlated states, started a new subfield of moire quantum materials. The originality and breadth are very high.
assessment.attribution: Bistritzer and MacDonald made the 2011 continuum-model prediction. Jarillo-Herrero's group made the decisive 2018 experimental discovery of insulating and superconducting states. This theory-plus-experiment configuration is clean, though other early or later contributors may be argued for, and I cannot verify the full credit history from the supplied text.
assessment.maturity: Reproduced by many groups across several moire systems, and the field is very active. The nature of the superconducting pairing is still debated, so the mechanism is not settled, but the discovery itself is robust. Timing is reasonable though the field is still evolving.
uncertainties: The microscopic mechanism of superconductivity and the correlated phases remains disputed.
Whether recognition should go to the 2011 theory, the 2018 experiments or both is a matter of committee judgement.
Credit among other early experimental and theoretical contributors is not fully resolved here.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Quantum key distribution turned the quantum measurement postulates into a practical cryptographic protocol (BB84) and an entanglement-based, Bell-inequality version (E91). It is original, conceptually clear and has produced lasting experimental programmes, and it follows naturally from the 2022 prize on entanglement and Bell tests.
assessment.attribution: Bennett and Brassard proposed BB84 in 1984; Ekert proposed the entanglement-based protocol in 1991. Pan is credited for large-scale experimental implementation (satellite and networks), but the four credited names exceed three, so a prize would need to choose. I propose the three originators of the protocols because the fundamental discovery is theoretical, while acknowledging that an experimental laureate could be argued for.
assessment.maturity: Protocols are decades old and widely implemented in commercial and national networks. Security proofs and device-independent variants are mature, though real-world implementations still face side-channel and distance limitations, so the engineering side is still developing.
uncertainties: Whether the prize should reward the theory, the experiments or both, and the exclusion of Pan under a three-person limit.
Practical security relative to quantum-resistant classical cryptography is a point of debate and not strictly a physics question.
Priority relationship to earlier ideas (for example Wiesner's conjugate coding) is acknowledged but I have not verified the details.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The 1995 Cirac-Zoller proposal for quantum gates with laser-cooled trapped ions, and its experimental realisation and scaling, established a leading platform for quantum computation with very high gate fidelities and long coherence. It is a foundational, original and clear contribution in atomic physics and quantum information.
assessment.attribution: Cirac and Zoller made the theoretical proposal; Blatt's group carried out a long series of experiments (gates, algorithms, entanglement of many ions). Wineland and Haroche were recognised in 2012 for quantum control of single systems, and Monroe and Wineland-group gate demonstrations are neighbouring contributions, so the allocation of experimental credit is not trivial.
assessment.maturity: The platform is well confirmed by independent groups and companies, with growing system sizes. Whether a useful quantum computer will result is not yet shown, so recognition would be for the physics of control, not for computational advantage.
uncertainties: The distinct credit for experimental work by Wineland, Monroe and others relative to Blatt.
Overlap with B035 and B028 for Cirac and Zoller; this entry is the more focused candidate.
Long-term scalability is still open.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The detection of high-energy astrophysical neutrinos with IceCube, including the diffuse flux and the association with the blazar TXS 0506+056 and the Galactic plane, created a new observational window with a km3 detector in Antarctic ice. This is a major experimental and conceptual achievement in astroparticle physics.
assessment.attribution: Halzen led the IceCube concept and collaboration; Karle is credited as a leading experimental figure. A large collaboration complicates a personal attribution, and other leaders (and the earlier Baikal and AMANDA efforts, and Koshiba and Davis awarded in 2002) are relevant context. The two-name configuration is workable but not obviously complete.
assessment.maturity: The diffuse flux is confirmed at high significance; the source identification is still developing, with only a few individual associations. The field is mature in detection but young in astrophysical interpretation.
uncertainties: Attribution within a very large collaboration is delicate and I cannot verify the full priority history.
Source identification remains incomplete, so the astrophysical meaning is still evolving.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The prediction of the quantum spin Hall effect in graphene and its Z2 classification by Kane and Mele, and the experimental observation in HgTe quantum wells, established topological insulators as a new phase of matter. The impact on condensed matter physics and on later topological band theory is very large and lasting.
assessment.attribution: Kane and Mele made the key theoretical proposals; Molenkamp's group made the first experimental observation (with the Zhang-group theory proposal for HgTe by Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang as an additional important contribution). Hasan, Moore and Balents, Fu, and Zhang are other credited contributors in this area, so the three-person limit is contested and I cannot resolve it from the supplied text.
assessment.maturity: Confirmed in many materials by independent groups. The topological band classification is stable, and recognition is not premature, but the 2016 prize on topological phase transitions and phases overlaps conceptually and could reduce the novelty.
uncertainties: Competing and overlapping credit (Bernevig, Hughes, Zhang, Fu, Moore, Hasan and others) is not resolved.
Overlap with B023, which differs in including Qi-Kun Xue and the quantum anomalous Hall effect.
Closeness to the 2016 topology prize.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Quantum simulation with ultracold atoms in optical lattices, including the observation of the superfluid-to-Mott-insulator transition and later quantum gas microscopes, provides controlled Hubbard-model physics and many-body dynamics. It is original and broadly influential, and conceptually close to my own field of atomic many-body physics.
assessment.attribution: Zoller (with Jaksch and collaborators) proposed the Hubbard-model realisation; Greiner and Bloch carried out the Mott transition and microscopy experiments. The proposers' coauthors, other microscope groups (Greiner, Bakr, Gross and Bloch) and the Cirac name in the supplied list create allocation questions.
assessment.maturity: Experimental techniques are well reproduced by many groups. Open questions such as solving the Fermi-Hubbard model at low temperature mean the long-term impact on solving problems is not yet settled, but the technique is already established.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2001 BEC prize and with B035 and B007 (the same theorists).
Whether quantum simulation has yet answered an open problem that a committee would regard as decisive.
Credit to Jaksch, Gross, Bakr and others is not in the supplied names.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Circuit quantum electrodynamics brought strong light-matter coupling to superconducting circuits and made the architecture for transmon-based quantum processors. The proposal and the first strong-coupling demonstration are original, clear and have lasting influence on quantum information science.
assessment.attribution: Blais, Huang, Wallraff, Girvin and Schoelkopf wrote the 2004 proposal; Wallraff and Schoelkopf with colleagues carried out the first experiments. Girvin and Devoret are major related contributors, and Devoret was part of the 2025 prize, so the credit boundary and overlap with the circuit-based 2025 recognition are material.
assessment.maturity: Mature and independently confirmed, with an industry-scale effort built on it. The 2025 prize on macroscopic quantum tunnelling in circuits makes an immediate follow-up less likely in terms of timing.
uncertainties: Proximity in time and subject to the 2025 prize.
Girvin's absence from the supplied names despite his role in the proposal.
Whether the committee wants a further circuit-related award so soon.
